business_problem: EDP Redes España needed to speed up electricity-network inspections, detect defects more accurately, and reduce the cost and environmental impact of manual review processes.
solution_summary: EDP Redes España and Capgemini replaced slow manual power-line inspections with an AI inspection stack built around computer vision, deep learning, and MLOps. The project began with a detailed review of inspection workflows, then introduced an MLOps platform that could train models from relatively small labeled datasets, plus an image-processing and inspection layer that attached geolocation data to network assets. The team used LandingAI and AWS technologies, first validating the approach in a proof of concept across three use cases and then extending it to nine more use cases in three countries. Helicopter images flow through the processing pipeline, AI models flag likely defects, and the inspection platform delivers prioritized results to field teams. Capgemini and EDP also ran change-management work so inspectors could adopt the new operating model without disrupting regular network maintenance.

data_flow: Helicopter inspection images are ingested and processed, geolocation is attached to the relevant assets, MLOps-managed computer-vision models analyze the imagery for defects, and the inspection platform returns prioritized findings to network inspection teams.
business_outcome: EDP Redes España cut inspection cycles dramatically, improved defect-detection accuracy, increased inspection frequency, and created a more scalable and lower-impact way to maintain network quality as electricity demand grows.

"The team opted for LandingAI and AWS technologies for the solution and began development with a proof of concept (PoC) that evaluated the AI models in three different use cases."
